questions.q: Why do vector databases usually use approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) indexes?
options: Exact search is mathematically impossible for vectors
Approximate indexes trade a little recall for much faster search at large scale
Approximate search always returns exactly the true top k
Exact search cannot use cosine similarity
questions.explain: Brute-force cost grows linearly with the number of vectors, so indexes skip most vectors and accept that a few true neighbors may be missed.

questions.q: What does recall@10 measure in the demo?
options: How many milliseconds ten queries take
The number of clusters searched
The fraction of the true top 10 neighbors that the approximate search returned
The dimensionality of the vectors
questions.explain: Recall@k compares the approximate results with the exact top k: 0.95 means 95 percent of the true top 10 were found.

questions.q: In the IVF-style index, what does increasing nprobe do?
options: Searches more clusters, improving recall but costing more time
Reduces the number of vectors stored
Changes the embedding model
Makes the search exact and always faster
questions.explain: nprobe is the number of clusters (cells) searched. In the demo recall rose from 0.71 to 1.00 as it went from 1 to 20, while time rose too.

questions.q: In the demo, nprobe=20 was slower than exact brute-force search. What does that illustrate?
options: The index code is wrong
Approximate search is always slower than exact search
Recall does not depend on nprobe
Index benefits depend on dataset size and settings; for modest data, exact search can be competitive
questions.explain: Exact search here is one fast matrix multiply on 50,000 vectors. Searching 20 clusters plus overhead can cost more. Gains grow with scale.

questions.q: Which is a sensible approach for a data scientist choosing a vector store?
options: Always buy the largest managed service first
Start with exact search or a library while validating embeddings, and adopt a database when you need scale, filtering, persistence, or concurrency
Never measure recall, since ANN is always perfect
Avoid metadata, since vector stores cannot filter
questions.explain: Validate that your embeddings work first, then add infrastructure for scale and features as needed, measuring recall on your own data.
